deliverables.verdict: The common recipe of the reference formats extracted as pure mechanics across ten sections: five-beat structure with one value change and one rope; the one-line-one-scene economy (8-14 words/line) governed by our measured F-25 spoken-load cap; quote-chained serialization with a hanger ledger and pay-on-open discipline; the worn stake (a readable number/state on the body, bargained against, with zero product support anywhere in the field); the funnel/vault conveyor (parts -> funnel shorts -> 30-45 min FULL STORY at 48-72h, compile-don't-regenerate); near-daily cadence with plan-ahead-in-threes; engagement hooks (EMPTY CAPTION poster-frame test, title-as-funnel grammar, participation with real consequences, public boards); the three-leg character-consistency stack (locked look / locked voice / persona rewritten per scene) with the four-class drift taxonomy; and the production discipline (hear/see before it moves, selective animation, cost shown before the burn). Every claim is cited to a source study section, and a closing gap-list section records what the whole field does NOT do - the layer that stays ours. No IP surface appears anywhere in the document.

All five morphed shows retooled at the format level, slate fixes (F1.1, F3.1-F3.4, F4.1, F5.1-F5.2) assumed landed. Slate-wide: episodes become quote-chained numbered PARTS with hanger ledgers, each show gains a FULL STORY vault plan on the 48-72h lag, titles gain the funnel grammar, cast accounting is published as boards, and each show names one viewer decision with a real next-part consequence. Per show: ON AIR becomes the serialized broadcast-night serial whose aired MV segment doubles as its funnel short, with COLONEL's invoice count as the worn stake; HOLD ON becomes the docket serial, the wall as public board, bell-counts as the bargained stake, viewer votes chalked onto the wall; THE NIGHT LIST becomes the nightly serial whose name board is run as a leaderboard, with nights-on-the-list as the stake and Door Test returns; ONE SHORT is the strongest fit - the count-along becomes formal audience participation whose posted count the office must answer, and the Counter wears his never-even streak; THE LAST SEAT is honestly flagged - it absorbs the outer layer (lease countdown worn on the house board, six nights as the part chain, poster-frame discipline, season vote tallied in the guest book) and refuses the inner line-economy layer on the record, because its danced-pair grammar is its proven asset and factory talking-head cadence would destroy it. Each show block includes the first E3 episode as a unit-by-unit skeleton retooled from its bible outline (no dialogue written), and a 'what stays ours' statement: base lore, ear-test, BLAM, E3 law, and the differentiator layer govern throughout.

The reusable playbook, written so a future agent can SLERM a new target format without re-deriving anything: the code-to-video analogy table (behavior -> artifacts, spec -> sauce, discard source -> quarantine surface, reimplement -> rebuild, behavior tests -> cold-watch gates); Step 0 name the prize; Step 1 study artifacts not marketing, with VERIFIED/INFERRED/LEAD grading and artifact-fingerprint pipeline reconstruction; Step 2 extract mechanics onto eight shelves plus a mandatory gap list, policed by the noun test (the spec must be statable without the target's proper nouns); Step 3 the discard pass with an explicit quarantine list and the reskin test; Step 4 rebuild from our cast cards under our law, with forced fits refused on the record; Step 5 seven cold-watch verification gates ending in the reskin check against the quarantine list; Step 6 banking - the SLERM is done when a second show can be retooled from the documents alone. Closes with six named failure modes, each drawn from the worked example (surface copying, mistaking the tool for the recipe, importing vendor constraints as mechanics, forcing the fit, skipping gates, letting a LEAD carry a decision).
